key_insight: MindView tests whether AI can generate spatially consistent new views of a scene from limited multi-view observations and language instructions. It introduces a benchmark with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets.
problem_solved: Existing generative spatial evaluations leave language-guided novel-view generation from partial multi-view observations underexplored.
method: Build a benchmark spanning 1,500 samples, 513 indoor scenes, and three datasets.
Organize seven tasks into two families, including geometry-dominant tasks that specify camera position and orientation changes.
Evaluate spatially consistent view generation guided by language and partial multi-view observations; the provided abstract is truncated and does not describe the second task family.
impact: MindView provides a structured way to assess spatial reasoning in generative models beyond image editing. It could help practitioners evaluate whether generated views preserve scene geometry under requested viewpoint changes.

paper_title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
paper_authors: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng
